$note: JSON Schema for WS /v1/stream frames. Tagged union discriminated on payload.kind. Generated from the Pydantic Envelope model.

Calibration.description:
Rolling-baseline health.

`healthy` going false must propagate and must suppress escalation. A stale
baseline produces confident nonsense.
Calibration.title: Calibration

CallState.description: State of the phone call to the 911 operator.
CallState.title: CallState

Claim.description: One assertion a sensing agent made about the building.

statement.description: Plain English, as caller would say it out loud.
statement.title: Statement

field.description: Which part of interior state it asserts, e.g. 'biometrics.respiration'.
field.title: Field

value.description: The asserted value, rendered as a string for display.
value.title: Value

Claim.title: Claim

ContextEvent.description: The resident's "what is happening" note, echoed back so the app can confirm delivery.
ContextEvent.title: ContextEvent

ContextNote.description:
One line the resident typed into the "what is happening" box.

Goes to master and becomes available to caller for the rest of the call.
Provenance is `user-input`: it is a human statement, not a measurement, and
caller must attribute it as such rather than asserting it as sensed fact.
ContextNote.title: ContextNote

EnvironmentReading.description:
Air quality. Carbon monoxide, and not from CSI.

CSI cannot sense gas composition at 2.4/5 GHz. This reading comes from a
separate modality, which is what makes it real corroboration rather than two
views of one stream. No gas sensor was purchased, so in practice
`provenance.source` is `demo-trigger` and `provenance.simulated` is true.
EnvironmentReading.title: EnvironmentReading

ErrorEvent.description: Something went wrong. Never silently drops a frame.
ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent

Floorplan.description: Static building geometry the 3D view draws. One resident, hardcoded.
Floorplan.title: Floorplan

HelloEvent.description: First frame on every connection. Tells the client what it just joined.

replay_from_seq.description: Sequence of the oldest event still buffered, for gap recovery.
replay_from_seq.title: Replay From Seq

HelloEvent.title: HelloEvent

Incident.description: One incident, from raised to resolved.

address.description: What the caller will read to the dispatcher.
address.title: Address

refusal_reason.description: Set when status is REFUSED: why the system declined to escalate.
refusal_reason.title: Refusal Reason

Incident.title: Incident

IncidentClassification.description:
Why master called it what it called it.

Classification is the interesting part and should be visible. A fall plus
elevated CO is a fire incident with a casualty, not a faint.

reasoning.description: Plain English, shown to the resident.
reasoning.title: Reasoning

discarded_claim_ids.description: Claims that did not survive verification. Named, not hidden.
discarded_claim_ids.title: Discarded Claim Ids

IncidentClassification.title: IncidentClassification

IncidentEvent.description: An incident was raised, classified, updated, resolved, or refused.
IncidentEvent.title: IncidentEvent

IncidentType.description: The three incident types. Nothing else classifies.
IncidentType.title: IncidentType

Instruction.description: One thing agents/guidance is telling the resident to do.

defers_to_operator.description: True when this instruction must be dropped the moment the dispatcher gives a competing one. Dispatchers are trained for this and the agent is not.
defers_to_operator.title: Defers To Operator

Instruction.title: Instruction

InstructionOrigin.description:
Where an instruction came from.

The UI should not distinguish these, because the user does not care. The API
does, because the safety rules differ: relayed operator instructions always
win over generated first aid.
InstructionOrigin.title: InstructionOrigin

InteriorState.description: Everything the app needs to draw the house right now.

associated_devices.description: Devices the router reports associated, hashed by the producer. An absent field means not reported, never that nobody is here.
associated_devices.title: Associated Devices

environment.description: Null when agents/environment has not reported.

InteriorState.title: InteriorState

Notice.description: One thing the resident should know about.

body.description: One line, composed by the producer from the zone and the floorplan's room name. Never the street address: the dispatch address is bound at registration and does not travel in a claim or in a notice. Enforced by construction in hawkeye_backend/notices/detector.py (Task 2), and asserted in the Twilio sink's tests (Task 3), rather than by a validator here - a heuristic content scan would fail on real room names.
body.title: Body

zone.description: Floorplan zone key, when there is one.
zone.title: Zone

room.description: The floorplan's display name for `zone`, e.g. 'Living room'. Resolved once by the producer so no consumer has to re-derive it or parse it back out of `body`.
room.title: Room

presence_id.description: Session-scoped only. We do not do person re-identification.
presence_id.title: Presence Id

Notice.title: Notice

NoticeEvent.description:
A notice was raised: something the resident should know about.

Does not create an incident and does not dial. `app/CLAUDE.md`: "An alert is
information a person acts on. It is not a call."
NoticeEvent.title: NoticeEvent

NoticeSeverity.description: How loudly the app should render it. Never a dispatch decision.
NoticeSeverity.title: NoticeSeverity

ObservedDevice.description:
A device seen associated to the network, hashed on arrival.

Carries `Provenance` because it is a reading like any other. On the mock
path that provenance says simulated, and nothing downstream has to guess.

identifier_hash.description: HMAC-SHA256 hex digest. Constrained here so a producer that base64s or truncates fails at the boundary rather than silently never matching.
identifier_hash.title: Identifier Hash

ObservedDevice.title: ObservedDevice

Position.description:
Coarse position inside the floorplan.

`zone` is the honest answer and is what the agents reason over. `x`/`y` exist
only so the 3D view has somewhere to draw; they are a zone centroid with
jitter, not a localization claim. Do not promise coordinates.

zone.description: Room-level zone id, e.g. 'main_bedroom'. Coarse by design.
zone.title: Zone

x.description: Metres from floorplan origin. Zone centroid, not a fix.
x.title: X

y.description: Metres from floorplan origin. Zone centroid, not a fix.
y.title: Y

Position.title: Position

Presence.description:
One tracked presence.

`presence_id` is stable within a session only. We do not do person
re-identification and must not claim to.

confidence.description: Confidence the presence exists at all.
confidence.title: Confidence

class_basis.description: What the class decision was made from. 'respiration_rate' is the defensible one.
class_basis.title: Class Basis

expected.description: agents/intruder's inference from context (entry point, time of day, count vs reported residents). Never a recognition result. null when not yet decided.
expected.title: Expected

still_down_s.description: Seconds down and not moving, from agents/collapse. The clinical variable: a long lie is over an hour, and half of those die within six months absent any injury.
still_down_s.title: Still Down S

Presence.title: Presence

PresenceClass.description:
Coarse class, decided from respiration rate, not signal amplitude.

Adult 12-20 BPM, child 20-30, infant 30-60, dog/cat 15-30+. The overlap
between child and pet is real and is stated rather than hidden; the honest
resolution is "adult versus small and fast-breathing".
PresenceClass.title: PresenceClass

PresenceState.description:
The three states app/CLAUDE.md requires the 3D view to distinguish.

CONFIRMED_MOVING: moving and breathing. A person, confirmed.
CONFIRMED_STILL:  still but breathing. A person who is not responding.
                  The loudest thing on screen. This is what the system exists for.
UNCONFIRMED:      a perturbation with no respiration signature. Render it as
                  such, not as a person. A curtain is not an intruder.
UNKNOWN:          not enough data yet. Absence of respiration is NOT proof of
                  absence of a person, so a presence that has not been
                  resolved sits here rather than being called UNCONFIRMED.
PresenceState.title: PresenceState

Provenance.description:
Where a reading came from. Required on every reading. No default.

`source_class` and `simulated` are computed from `source`, so a producer
cannot claim a demo-trigger reading was measured.

source.description: What physically produced this reading. Required.

producer.description: Which agent or component emitted it, e.g. 'agents/environment'.
producer.title: Producer

ansname.description: ANSName of the producing agent, when it has one.
ansname.title: Ansname

detail.description: Free text, e.g. the capture session id a replay came from.
detail.title: Detail

source_class.description: Derived from `source`. Never supplied by the caller.

simulated.description:
True when this number was not measured by any instrument.

The iOS app renders a badge off this. It is derived, so it cannot lie.
simulated.title: Simulated

Provenance.title: Provenance

RaisedBy.description:
Who raised it.

USER is the only path to a call. Hawk Eye never dials 911 on its own;
settled 2026-09-19. A human tap is what releases `agents/caller` to dial,
and `agents/collapse` and `agents/environment` surface their detections as
interior state the resident acts on rather than as a call.

SYSTEM is kept for wire compatibility and for records raised before that
decision. It must never reach the dialing path: `assert_human_released` in
`master/base.py` enforces that structurally rather than by convention.
RaisedBy.title: RaisedBy

RespirationStatus.description: Respiration is the personhood test. Never heart rate.
RespirationStatus.title: RespirationStatus

Room.description: One room in the floorplan. Polygon in metres, floorplan origin at (0,0).
Room.title: Room

Source.description:
What physically produced a reading.

Closed set on purpose. Adding a value is a deliberate act, and each new value
must be placed into MEASURED_SOURCES or SIMULATED_SOURCES below.
Source.title: Source

SourceAgent.description: The agent that made the claim.

ansname.description: The ANSName the claim was presented under.
ansname.title: Ansname

certificate_version.description: Version-bound certificate recording the code running at registration. A fingerprint that drifted mid-run is how code drift becomes detectable.
certificate_version.title: Certificate Version

SourceAgent.title: SourceAgent

SourceClass.description:
How much weight a reading's origin can bear.

Derived from `Source`, never supplied. This is the field the iOS app renders
a "simulated" badge from.
SourceClass.title: SourceClass

StateEvent.description: An interior state tick. Roughly 2 Hz during an incident, 0.5 Hz otherwise.
StateEvent.title: StateEvent

TranscriptEvent.description: One line of the caller <-> 911 conversation.
TranscriptEvent.title: TranscriptEvent

TranscriptLine.description:
One line of the caller <-> 911 conversation, shown to the resident.

The operator does not see this. It exists so the resident is not left in
silence while a synthetic voice speaks on their behalf.

final.description: False for a partial transcription being revised in place. Match on line_id.
final.title: Final

claim_ids.description: Verified claims this line repeats. Lets the app link a spoken sentence to its proof.
claim_ids.title: Claim Ids

TranscriptLine.title: TranscriptLine

TranscriptSpeaker.description:
Who said a line.

CALLER is our agent's synthesized voice. OPERATOR is the human dispatcher.
RESIDENT appears when the resident speaks on the line directly.
SYSTEM is a non-speech annotation, e.g. "call connected".
TranscriptSpeaker.title: TranscriptSpeaker

TrustIndexScore.description:
Trust Index scores at the instant the claim was verified.

Only integrity and identity are implemented upstream. Solvency, behavior and
safety are hardcoded to 0 in the reference implementation, so they are
nullable here rather than silently zero: a 0 that means "not implemented"
and a 0 that means "scored zero" are different facts and the app must not
conflate them. ans/CLAUDE.md names safety as the dimension we intend to ship.

unimplemented_dimensions.description: Dimensions the Trust Index does not yet score. Null above, named here.
unimplemented_dimensions.title: Unimplemented Dimensions

TrustIndexScore.title: TrustIndexScore

TrustProfile.description:
Trust Index `recommendedProfile` policy hint.

Consumed rather than reinvented. Using the track's own policy vocabulary is
free credibility, and the mapping to what a claim may trigger is the table in
agents/CLAUDE.md.
TrustProfile.title: TrustProfile

VerificationCheck.title: VerificationCheck

VerificationDecision.description:
What master did with a claim, given the source's profile.

| Profile       | Decision            | Meaning                                        |
|---------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| UNTRUSTED     | DISCARDED           | Discards. Logs. Does not relay.                |
| READ_ONLY     | CORROBORATION_ONLY  | Never the sole basis for a call.               |
| TRANSACTIONAL | ATTRIBUTED          | Relayed as a reported observation, attributed. |
| FIDUCIARY     | ASSERTED            | Relayed as an assertion the system stands behind. |

DISCARDED is also the decision when any check fails, whatever the profile.
VerificationDecision.title: VerificationDecision

VerificationEvent.description:
An ANS verification result: which claim, which agent, verified or DISCARDED and why.

This event is the submission. A demo that escalates is unremarkable; one that
correctly refuses an impostor is the point, and the app renders that refusal
off this event.
VerificationEvent.title: VerificationEvent

VerificationResult.description: A claim, who made it, what was checked, and what was decided.

reason.description: Why this decision. Required even on ASSERTED, so the stream reads the same both ways.
reason.title: Reason

will_be_spoken.description: Whether agents/caller is permitted to repeat this claim to the operator.
will_be_spoken.title: Will Be Spoken

VerificationResult.title: VerificationResult

Vitals.description: Respiration and heart rate. Respiration carries the personhood verdict.

breathing_bpm.description: RuView's stated range. Outside 6-30, report null rather than a number.
breathing_bpm.title: Breathing Bpm

heart_bpm.description: Stretch goal, and a good number to say on the call. Never the personhood test.
heart_bpm.title: Heart Bpm

person_confidence.description: Confidence that this perturbation is a living body.
person_confidence.title: Person Confidence

Vitals.title: Vitals

schema.description: Every websocket frame is one of these.

seq.description: Monotonic, server-wide. A gap means the client missed a frame.
seq.title: Seq

incident_id.description: Set when the event belongs to an incident.
incident_id.title: Incident Id

schema.title: Envelope
